decisions.reason: Each public StartupReleaseManifest.verify/verifyCandidate allocates a fresh package-private ReleasePayloadVerification immediately for its own synchronous verify invocation. jars is a private final builder populated only in walk then consumed by agreement; it and its owner never return. Output Contents contains newly collected unmodifiable metadata, not this builder. Concurrent public invocations have separate builder owners; ConcurrentHashMap would not make a shared/reused verifier operation coherent and is unnecessary under the actual fresh-owner contract.
requiredDynamicPostconditions: Two concurrent verify operations use distinct builders and no mutable-map escape
Actual retained directory/manifest/BOM/signature checks remain unperformed and held

decisions.reason: The private final checksum map is allocated with the per-invocation verifier owner in each of the only two constructor sites. walk inserts immutable Integer checksums synchronously and agreement reads after traversal; no map or verifier escapes into returned Contents. There is no shared mutable checksum map across concurrent verify/verifyCandidate calls. This source finding is confined to map choice, not actual filesystem/signature/BOM acceptance.
requiredDynamicPostconditions: Two concurrent verify operations use distinct builders and no mutable-map escape
Actual retained directory/manifest/BOM/signature checks remain unperformed and held

decisions.reason: WebManagementServer writes started=true only after server.start returns while stopLock is held. promote/ready and stopFailure observe it; ready/promote do not acquire stopLock. volatile supplies visibility of successful start to these readers, while AtomicBoolean stopping/promoted and stopLock control other transitions. It is not used for a compound read-modify-write or as evidence that an unknown stop released selector/socket. The normal stop contract still separately requires actual termination.
requiredDynamicPostconditions: Independent concurrent start/ready/close histories with actual provider outcome; no tuple linearizability inferred
Ownership retained on partial startup and unknown cleanup; budgets/interrupt/real socket or worker termination remain unperformed

decisions.reason: WebNativeRuntime start owns ownerLock and captures bind result before listener start can fail. healthy copies this volatile reference once outside ownerLock; close holds ownerLock and retains the owner for cleanup. The field publishes an acquired owner, not an already-ready graph; the health predicate separately checks ready/stopping/terminal. No compound update relies on volatile.
requiredDynamicPostconditions: Independent concurrent start/ready/close histories with actual provider outcome; no tuple linearizability inferred
Ownership retained on partial startup and unknown cleanup; budgets/interrupt/real socket or worker termination remain unperformed

decisions.reason: Under ownerLock startup publishes the returned replay worker; healthy takes a local reference outside that lock and close uses the retained owner. volatile provides that single-handle publication only. Actual worker running/stop/join and all budget postconditions remain separate; no aggregate readiness or completed cleanup is inferred.

decisions.reason: Under ownerLock startup captures the revocation retry worker; healthy and close each snapshot the reference. volatile provides visibility without claiming atomicity with other runtime handles, retry completion, a permit, or native termination. decisions.reason: ArtemisReplyConsumers close writes stopping=true under stateLock before context.close; ready observes it without taking stateLock and must refuse stopping. volatile makes this stop fence visible. closed/startAttempted are instead lock-guarded, and atomic terminal/halted are separate signals. No provider close completion or compound linearizable readiness snapshot is inferred.
requiredDynamicPostconditions: Independent concurrent start/ready/close histories with actual provider outcome; no tuple linearizability inferred
